title: RAP: Resource-aware Automated GPU Sharing for Multi-GPU Recommendation Model Training and Input Preprocessing
problem: Current DLRM retraining systems require hundreds of CPU nodes for input preprocessing, consuming more power than GPU training itself, creating significant resource inefficiency and operational overhead.
motivation: Optimizing GPU resource utilization and reducing preprocessing power consumption is critical for scalable online recommendation model retraining.
method: RAP consolidates two jobs on the same GPU instead of separate machines: training a recommendation model (predicting what users want) and preparing the input data that feeds into it. The system automatically allocates GPU time between the two tasks based on how much work each requires at any moment. This eliminates the need for hundreds of dedicated CPU nodes currently used just for data preparation—which consume more power than the GPU training itself.
key_novelty: Instead of requiring separate CPU infrastructure for data preparation, this system lets a single GPU handle both model training and data preparation by automatically splitting its time based on what each task needs at any moment.
contributions: Automated framework for GPU sharing between training and preprocessing workloads
Resource-aware scheduling mechanism for efficient GPU allocation
Elimination of large CPU preprocessing clusters in DLRM retraining pipelines
Multi-GPU coordination strategy for online model retraining
limitations: Specific performance improvements, scalability limits, and evaluation results are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: GPU sharing for recommendation model training
